historical_references.reference: The name Itishaa is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ishana', which means 'Lord of All'. It was a common name in ancient India, particularly among the Hindu populace. It is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas. In the Mahabharata, Itishaa is the name of a sage who was a disciple of the great sage Vyasa. He is revered for his deep devotion and wisdom.

Another reference to the name Itishaa can be found in the works of the 12th century poet Jayadeva. In his famous work 'Gita Govinda', Itishaa is depicted as a name of Krishna, the god of love and joy. Krishna is described as being the source of all happiness and pleasure, and the name Itishaa signifies that aspect of the deity.
